data.exact_reserve_text:
The prior accident year experience has been less benign. Deterioration on the earned and booked position on some accounts has had a negative impact on the Syndicate's result for the year. In particular, deterioration on certain Marine Insurance segments has dragged back the performance of this class. Corrective action has now been applied to this account to restructure its composition and return it to the profitable performance it has historically produced.
The legacy Solicitor's Professional Indemnity portfolio, from which the Syndicate has now exited, also exhibited some deterioration in the first half of the calendar year based on claims development on prior years' exposures. Recent development has been more stable but reserves have nonetheless been strengthened.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate's opening gross claims outstanding at 1 Jan 2015 was GBP 418.878m. During 2015 there was material prior-year favourable development on gross claims (a net release of c. GBP 289.99m gross), resulting in a large net release overall despite pockets of deterioration on some prior-year exposures (notably certain Marine segments and a legacy Solicitor's PI portfolio where reserves were strengthened). The net effect reported in the claims reconciliation is a significant gross release, but the Managing Agent also notes specific adverse developments in selected accounts which were addressed.

data.data_quality_notes: Primary opening reserve taken from balance sheet claims outstanding (prior-year comparative). Prior-year movement sourced from the claims reconciliation note line 'Claims incurred in prior accident years' (gross GBP (289,988)k) which is presented in the claims outstanding movement schedule; this line was used as the movement in prior-years reserves. The claims development triangle is present but includes an aggregated '2011 & Prior' column which was excluded per rules; RITC activity (2013 YOA reinsured to close) is noted in the report and may distort the triangle/older year comparatives. Some narrative describes deterioration on specific accounts while the reconciliation shows a net gross release - this mix means portfolio-level and class-level movements differ.
